# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate invalidates a stored audit when ANY of its content-fingerprint components change: git HEAD sha, work-item description hash, Key Files list, and working-tree state (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`). Because the fingerprint includes the **whole-repo** git HEAD sha and working-tree state, a commit to dev from an *unrelated* work item (or any uncommitted/untracked file change) invalidates every stored audit in the worklog and re-triggers the full audit pipeline — even though the audited item itself never changed.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** the item was audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD `310773d5`. Afterward, an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged `aaabdede` to dev. The content fingerprint changed (verified: stored `58947e06…` matches recomputation at `310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), so the audit went stale, the re-audit ran, and it blocked on the pre-flight full-suite cache gate — leaving a verified "Ready to close: Yes" item stuck in review.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity doesn't invalidate my audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data only** — the work item's description (which contains the ACs and the Key Files section) plus its title. The **git HEAD sha and working-tree-state components are removed** from the fingerprint entirely (no git calls in the computation).
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test: fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored audit. Regression test: fingerprint is stable across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content).
6. **Migration of legacy v1 reports:** reports persisted before this change carry fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formula that cannot be recomputed. Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`) so legacy lines are distinguishable; legacy reports fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt + `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`) — **no silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (only used by the fingerprint) is removed; `_resolve_audited_head` stays (still used by green-run attestation).
8. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate section ~line 134), `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~line 95), and the code docstrings on `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` / `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved).
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls through to a full re-audit (existing behavior).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR, lines ~3877/6056/6391) uses the same fingerprint — it must keep working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~1034) — payload = `{head_sha, description_hash, key_files, working_tree_hash}`.
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~913) — content gate primary; time gate floor for fingerprint-less legacy reports.
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (line ~1080) — only used by the fingerprint (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line 431); embedded at lines ~3256/3281/3538.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — fingerprint tests at ~7791-7913 (HEAD sha, description, key files, working-tree states), freshness-gate tests (~2252, 3798-3813, 4275).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness gate behavior section (line ~134).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness gate summary (line ~95).
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this; covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint` (simplify), `_check_audit_freshness` (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, remove `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update fingerprint/freshness tests (~7791-7913, 2252, 3798-3813, 4275)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary line

## Related work

- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (in_review) — the working-tree component this item REMOVES (this item supersedes that component).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (done) — introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (in_review) — the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy v1 reports fall back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD churn thereafter. Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence:** dropping the git components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it (e.g. another work item edits a Key File). Accepted by design per this item's rule; the audit's verdict remains the record for the item's own data.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit? — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer: remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.
data.title: Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change

# Intake Brief — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H)

## Problem Statement

When the audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) completes an audit with a "Ready to close: Yes" verdict, it advances the item to `completed`/`in_review` but does **not** set the `needsProducerReview` flag. The producer-review gate (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in the ship skill skips items with `needsProducerReview: true`) is therefore bypassed for auto-audited items. However, the flag should only be set for **top-level** items (no parent): child items are covered by their parent's producer review, and marking every child for review would flood the producer queue with redundant approvals. The previous blanket behavior (set the flag for all items, SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW) was dropped during a later refactor (SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM), so this item restores the gating with the top-level-only refinement.

## Users

- **Producers / maintainers** — need assurance that every top-level completed work item proceeds to release only after their explicit review, without being buried by redundant child-item review requests.
- **AI agents running audits** — currently produce `completed` status without the `needsProducerReview` flag, creating a gap in the release gating chain for top-level items.

### User Stories

- **As a** Producer, **I want** every top-level item that an automated audit marks as "ready to close" to also have `needsProducerReview: true`, **so that** I can review it before release.
- **As a** Producer, **I want** child items to be **excluded** from the producer-review flag, **so that** I only review top-level items (their parent's review covers the subtree).
- **As an** AI agent running `/skill:audit`, **I want** the audit runner to set `--needs-producer-review yes` only when the item has no parent, **so that** release gating is enforced without queue flooding.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1**: When `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` in `audit_runner.py` applies a "yes" verdict (`status=completed`, `stage=in_review`) and the audited item has **no parent** (`parentId` is null/empty), the terminal `wl update` includes `--needs-producer-review yes`.
2. **AC2**: When the audited item **has a parent** (`parentId` set), the terminal `wl update` for a "yes" verdict does **not** include `--needs-producer-review` (the flag is left unchanged).
3. **AC3**: The "no" verdict and failure/restore branches never set `--needs-producer-review` (behavior unchanged).
4. **AC4**: Unit tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` verify both cases (top-level sets the flag; child does not), and the full audit test suite passes with no regressions.
5. **AC5**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (Status Lifecycle section) and code comments.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The change is localized to the standalone audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) — the AMPA engine's audit handler (separate code path, `docs/triage-audit.md`) is unaffected.
- Backward compatibility: the "no" and failure/restore paths must behave exactly as before.
- The flag must be set **only** on a genuine "Yes" verdict for top-level items — never on failure/fallback runs.
- No modifications to `.pi/` or agent-infrastructure directories outside the SorraAgents repo.

## Existing State

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (circa line 6740–6790): the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch builds `["wl", "update", <id>, "--status", "completed", "--stage", "in_review", "--json"]` — no `--needs-producer-review` flag is ever passed. (The flag was added by SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW but dropped in commit `3c876e1e`, SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM.)
- `ctx.wi` (the work item dict captured via `wl show <id> --json` in `_phase_gate`) includes `parentId` — `None` for top-level items, the parent's id for children.
- `wl update` CLI supports `--needs-producer-review <true|false>` (confirmed via `wl update --help`).
- Tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` assert the exact terminal `wl update` command; the mock runner returns a `workItem` without `parentId` (treated as top-level), so existing "yes" tests will need the flag expectation added.

## Desired Change

1. **`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`** — In `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, in the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch, when `ctx.wi.get("parentId")` is falsy (top-level item), append `--needs-producer-review yes` to the `restore_cmd` (both the `done`-stage and normal `in_review` variants). When the item has a parent, leave the command unchanged.
2. **Tests** — Update `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` "yes"-verdict tests to expect `--needs-producer-review yes` (top-level default), and add a test where the mock work item has a `parentId` asserting the flag is absent.
3. **Docs** — Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` Status Lifecycle section (bullet + Manual Fallback commands) to note that a "Yes" verdict also sets `needsProducerReview` for top-level items only.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (Phase 6, `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch, ~line 6770). Needs a parent check (`ctx.wi.get("parentId")`) before appending `--needs-producer-review yes`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — `TestVerdictDrivenStatusLifecycle`; `_make_runner` helper (add optional `parent_id`), and the three "yes" tests plus a new child-item test.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle section (line ~35) documents the `Yes` → `completed`/`in_review` transition; add the producer-review note.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

1. **Gate regressions:** If the flag is accidentally set for child items (or missed for top-level), the release gate either blocks release with redundant reviews or lets top-level items ship unreviewed. **Mitigation:** unit tests cover both branches explicitly; the change is a single conditional append.
2. **Scope creep:** The intent is strictly the audit runner's terminal transition. Extending the flag semantics to the AMPA engine, `persist_audit.py`, or batch skills is out of scope. **Mitigation:** keep the change localized; file separate work items for any follow-ups.
3. **`parentId` availability:** If `ctx.wi` were ever absent/empty, the check must default to top-level (set the flag) rather than silently skipping it. **Mitigation:** treat a missing/empty `parentId` as top-level (falsy check).

### Assumptions

- "Top-level item" = `parentId` is `null`/empty in the work item JSON — confirmed present on `wl show <id> --json` output.
- Child items' `needsProducerReview` flag is left **unchanged** (not force-cleared): the requirement says only that the marking happens "IF and only if" the item is top-level. A child already flagged (e.g., by AMPA) keeps its flag.
- The AMPA engine's `close_with_audit` handler already sets `--needs-producer-review true` via a separate code path and is unaffected by this change.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** (completed) — "Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks item as ready to close": the original blanket implementation, later dropped in SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM; this item restores it with the top-level-only refinement.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPG003OFYO** (completed) — "Filter closeWorkItemsAfterRelease by needsProducerReview": the downstream gate that this flag feeds.
- **SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS** (completed) — "Close work items after release only when readyToClose and producerReview conditions are met": release-time gating semantics.
- **SA-0MSAWFTZX003T042** (completed) — "Audit completion must set status: open (readyToClose: no) or completed (readyToClose: yes)": the verdict-driven lifecycle this change extends.
- **SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM** (completed) — "Fix hardcoded DEFAULT_MODEL 'Proxy/qwen3' in audit runner": the refactor (commit `3c876e1e`) that dropped the flag from the runner.
- **SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I** (completed) — "If a child audit is not ready to close then the parent must also be marked as not ready to close": parent/child audit consistency context.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Should child items get `--needs-producer-review no` explicitly, or be left unchanged?" — Answer (operator, via seed intent): "Marked as needing producer review IF, and only if, the item is a top level item". Interpretation: the flag is only ever set (to `yes`) for top-level items; child items are left untouched. Source: interactive request. Research: `wl update` supports an explicit flag, but force-clearing child flags could clobber flags set by other flows (e.g. AMPA) — documented as an assumption above.
- Q2: "Does this replace the previous blanket behavior from SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW?" — Answer (inferred from seed intent + git history): yes — the previous implementation set the flag for all items and was subsequently dropped; this item restores it with the top-level-only condition. Source: `git log -S needsProducerReview`, commit `3c876e1e`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQJONW3C007SZQY** – Audit runner: manage work item status during audit execution (completed)
- **SA-0MQA6ECEU003GUKH** – PlanAll: Automated Batch Planning for intake_complete items (completed)
- **SA-0MS3AU0LH002GCZK** – [HIGH] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:1 — Shebang is present but file is not executable (EXE001) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-audit-pass-set-needsProducerReview-only-for-top-level-items-SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H.md` — matched: audit, completes, intent, item, items, level, marked, needing, needsproducerreview, parent, pass, passes, producer, review, seed, set, should, top, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSQ8MXXI0029B5M-fix-child-verdict-test-contract/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: audit, completes, high, intent, item, items, level, marked, needing, parent, pass, passes, priority, review, set, should, top, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRM48PL006TH8Q-test-non-owning-cwd-git-resolution/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: audit, completes, high, intent, item, items, level, marked, needing, parent, pass, passes, priority, review, set, should, top, when

# Docs: READ-ONLY exception + audit-skill-reference update (docs)

Part of SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR (Phase D — finalize). Completes AC5: document the justified READ-ONLY exception and the new behavior, and confirm the full project test suite passes.

## Goal

The audit skill's SKILL.md (READ-ONLY safety section + the "Do NOT close, create, or delete work items" rule) and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` precisely document the exception, the false-positive screen, the remediation loop, the chore-item creation, and any new flags/env vars — and the full project test suite passes with all changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` READ-ONLY section documents the exception scope exactly: config-file write, local commit, chore-item creation, code-quality re-run only; all other phases remain read-only; the audit still never closes or deletes work items and never pushes.

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
data.title: Audit runner: filter non-Python files before passing to ruff

## Blocker: wl sync refuses to pull refs/worklog/data

**Symptom**

`wl sync` fails with: `✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 117 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.`

Categories (from `wl sync debug` + gate output):
- ~108 commits: **empty author email** (author 'Sorra the Orc', no email) — latest Aug 15 20:28; earliest Aug 13-14 range
- ~9 commits: author email `ross@example.com` does not match configured user.email `pi@local`

`--allow-foreign-author` does NOT help: it explicitly 'never bypasses the empty-author-email gate', and the majority of commits are empty-email.

**Impact**

- No pull/push sync for the SorraAgents worklog at all — changes accumulate locally only (work items/comments land in the local sqlite store but never reach the git ref or remote); the remote diverges.
- New local items (e.g. SA-0MSW9Q08A0045GRV) cannot be pushed.
- Affects all SorraAgents wl operations relying on sync.

**Likely root cause / remediation options (to be investigated)**

1. Remote ref history was authored by an environment with no git user.email configured (empty), or with `ross@example.com` (some other machine config), while the local store uses `pi@local` (config.yaml / git config mismatch).
2. If the remote ref is the canonical history, rewrite/filter the ref (git filter-branch / git filter-repo author fix) so all commits carry the configured identity, then re-sync.
3. Check whether the wl store config (user.email) used to be `ross@example.com` in another working copy and whether 2) is safe; do NOT force-push without operator approval.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `wl sync` in SorraAgents completes successfully (pulls remote worklog data).
2. The author-identity gate passes for all commits on refs/worklog/data (no empty emails, no foreign emails).
3. Local items (e.g. SA-0MSW9Q08A0045GRV) push to the remote ref.
4. A documented decision on how future commits avoid empty-author-email (git config user.email enforcement / wl gate).

## Problem

render_report.py::render_ac_table only checks for the met boolean field and defaults to unmet for anything else. The audit runner passes AC results with a verdict field containing values like adjusted, partial, met, unmet. When an AC has verdict: adjusted, render_ac_table sees row.get(met) as None (falsy) and renders it as unmet, losing the important adjusted/partial distinction.

## Root cause

render_report.py line 224:
  verdict = "met" if row.get("met") else "unmet"

This only checks the met key. Rows from the audit runner contain verdict with values like adjusted or partial, but no met key.

## Fix

Update render_ac_table to check for verdict first, then fall back to met boolean for backward compatibility.

## Acceptance criteria

1. render_ac_table renders adjusted, partial, met, and unmet verdicts correctly
2. Backward compatibility: rows with only met: True/False still work
3. Tests cover all four verdict values plus the met-boolean fallback
data.title: fix: render_report.py doesn't handle 'adjusted'/'partial' AC verdicts

## Goal

Prevent ruff (the Python linter) from mis-parsing YAML and other non-Python configuration files as Python source, which produces false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that pollute the Quality Improvement epic as auto-created work items. The fix MUST be **additive**: it must not hardcode any project-specific path (e.g. `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`), must not break scanning of other projects, and must never hide genuine Python findings in `.py` files in any project.

## Background / Root cause

The llm project Quality Improvement epic **LP-0MT1F4IQU00828FC** accumulated **155 false-positive child work items** (2026-08-20), all ruff `invalid-syntax` errors reported against `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — a YAML file being linted as Python (Unexpected indentation, Invalid annotated assignment target, Expected an expression, etc.).

The existing explicit-file-argument filter (commit e910f02d, `_run_ruff_check` / `_run_ruff_fix_mode`) only excludes TS/JS extensions and only in the `files=` branch. Two gaps remain:
1. The **whole-project scan path** (`files=None`, the `else` branch) runs `ruff check <root>` with only a TS/JS `--extend-exclude` — it does NOT exclude `.yaml`/`.yml` or other non-Python config files.
2. The current exclusion list is English-agnostic about additivity — it must be extended to cover non-Python config extensions generically so the fix holds for ANY project (not just llm), while never suppressing genuine findings.

Related existing item: **SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5** addresses the explicit-file-argument path in the audit runner. This item covers the whole-project scan path and generalises the exclusion so it is additive across all projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The whole-project ruff scan path (`files=None`) excludes non-Python configuration extensions (at minimum `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.md`) so ruff never mis-parses them, via `--extend-exclude`/`--force-exclude` — not by hardcoding any project-specific filename.
2. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected: existing tests pass and no Python lint is suppressed.
3. The fix is additive — works for any project root (verified with a non-llm project containing a `.yaml` file), with no hardcoded absolute paths or project names in the exclusion logic.
4. A regression test asserts that scanning a project tree containing a `.yaml` file (both a whole-project scan and an explicit-file scan) produces zero findings for that YAML file, while a `.py` file with a genuine issue still yields its finding.
5. The change is documented in the linter_runner module docstring/comment (both the explicit-file and whole-project paths).
data.title: Ruff: exclude YAML & non-Python files additively across all projects (whole-project scan)

## Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

## Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

## Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

## Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.
data.title: Audit: parent-first flow re-audits stale children and blocks on unserviced in-main-slot verdicts
